videos.title: Strength Check with Guy Tanapat  & Yuri Chub
videos.summary:
It's been so long since I had a strength check, and this one was overdue. I'm at Muscle Factory gym in Bangkok with Guy Tanapat and Yuri Chub, and we get some real table time in.

I introduce Guy as Thailand's number one, then we grip up. First pulls and a strap with Guy, then Yuri comes in: tall, long-levered, and a constant climber. Guy talks through his left and right, and prefers a hook on the left. After that we go ready go with Yuri, fight over the webbing and the buckle, and I have to make him come low because I can't match his hand.

I also look at the King's move as a backup for when the hand is blown up and I can't go sideways. I've never won a match from it, but I can hold people off for a long time, which is useful in a supermatch. Guy's got a real press, and that changes everything. When I faced Eldar Bubenko in round three, I found he didn't have a press, so I could tie him up. You can't do that with Guy.

Yuri is a problem in the best way: climbing, rising, and taking the webbing. At 105 kg, big, tall and long-levered, if he gets his hand away he knows how to shut down your side pressure and twist through, and you don't get that palm-based side pressure activated. In a competition against someone like that, you have to talk to the referee and not give away that extra inch of webbing.

videos.title: The Pound for Pound Podcast Episode 5: Shahil Hussain, Multiple National Gold Medalist of India
videos.summary:
Pound for Pound Podcast Episode 5: Ryan Bowen sits down with Shahil Hussain, multiple national gold medalist of India, Pound for Pound supermatch contender and a legend of Nagaon armwrestling.

Shahil shares how he found armwrestling at 16 in Nagaon, Assam, learned from internet cafes and local mentors, and built a scene where dozens of kids come to his house every Sunday to pull. He talks through his first nationals in Mathura, his first national gold in Hyderabad in 2022, and what his Eliza Cup supermatch against Jamie Barrett taught him about explosiveness, centre control and the mental game.

Ryan and Shahil also get into side pressure, why wrist size matters less than you think, a visit to an Istanbul club with 250 world titles in the room, facing bigger opponents without fear, armwrestling as a bone sport, and why conditioning beats chasing big numbers.
